evidence.title: Beyond Views: Measuring and Predicting Engagement in Online Videos
evidence.abstract: The share of videos in the internet traffic has been growing, therefore understanding how videos capture attention on a global scale is also of growing importance. Most current research focus on modeling the number of views, but we argue that video engagement, or time spent watching is a more appropriate measure for resource allocation problems in attention, networking, and promotion activities. In this paper, we present a first large-scale measurement of video-level aggregate engagement from publicly available data streams, on a collection of 5.3 million YouTube videos published over two months in 2016. We study a set of metrics including time and the average percentage of a video watched. We define a new metric, relative engagement, that is calibrated against video properties and strongly correlate with recognized notions of quality. Moreover, we find that engagement measures of a video are stable over time, thus separating the concerns for modeling engagement and those for popularity -- the latter is known to be unstable over time and driven by external promotions. We also find engagement metrics predictable from a cold-start setup, having most of its variance explained by video context, topics and channel information -- R2=0.77. Our observations imply several prospective uses of engagement metrics -- choosing engaging topics for video production, or promoting engaging videos in recommender systems.

evidence.title: Reaching Diverse Groups in Long-Term Astronomy Public Engagement Efforts
evidence.abstract: Professional astronomy is historically not an environment of diverse identities. In recognizing that public outreach efforts affect career outcomes for young people, it is important to assess the demographics of those being reached and continually consider strategies for successfully engaging underrepresented groups. One such outreach event, the International Astronomical Youth Camp (IAYC), has a 50-year history and has reached ~1700 participants from around the world. We find that the IAYC is doing well in terms of gender (59% female, 4.7% non-binary at the most recent camp) and LGBT+ representation, whereas black and ethnic minorities are lacking. In this proceeding, we report the current landscape of demographics applying to and attending the IAYC; the efforts we are making to increase diversity amongst participants; the challenges we face; and our future plans to bridge these gaps, not only for the benefit of the camp but for society overall.

evidence.title: Research of Economical Shift Rule of Automatic Power Shift Transmission of Tractor
evidence.abstract: When working at light load operation（ such as sowing,weeding,transplanting,harvesting,etc.）,the traditional tractor has the problem of low power utilization ratio and high fuel consumption. Through analyzing the best economy index and its influence factors of tractor,a kind of economical shift rule is put forward,which based on the minimum fuel consumption rate of tractor. It requires not only the operating point of the engine located at the lowest fuel consumption zone,also need the tractor traction efficiency to be higher. For this reason,the slip rate of driving wheel is introduced to constitute economical shift rule and its control strategy,which takes the speed,drive wheel speed,engine speed,throttle opening and transmission gear ratio of tractor as control parameters. The fuzzy control is used to identify the driving intention,and the driver intervention on the shifting process is introduced to the transmission control,which can reflect the actual working environment of the tractor. Taking the YTO LA2004 wheeled tractor which equipped with automatic power shift transmission as investigative subject,the simulation analysis of light load working condition is carried out. The results show that the gear and throttle opening change with traction load,which ensure that the working point of the engine is in a low fuel consumption zone. The fuel consumption rate of tractor is reduced and the stability of the actual speed of the tractor is achieved. A theoretical basis for the development of automatic transmission control system of tractor is provided by the research

evidence.title: Research on Transmission Characteristic of ZF 9-speed Automatic Transmission
evidence.abstract: Taking the ZF 9-speed automatic transmission (9HP48) as the research object，the power transmission line in each gear of the automatic transmission is clarified. The transmission ratio and torque ratio (considering friction loss) of each gear are theoretically derived. The М.А.Крейнeс formula is used to calculate the transmission efficiency of 9 forward gears and 1 reverse gear. To verify the theoretical derivation，AMESim simulation software is used for building the simulation model of the automatic transmission. The transmission ratio and transmission efficiency values of each gear are obtained through the simulation calculation. The simulation results are consistent with the theoretical analysis results. The simulation results verify the correctness of the theoretical derivation and provide a basis for optimizing the automatic transmission scheme in the future

system.value: Research of Economical Shift Rule of Automatic Power Shift Transmission of Tractor

abstract.value: When working at light load operation（ such as sowing,weeding,transplanting,harvesting,etc.）,the traditional tractor has the problem of low power utilization ratio and high fuel consumption. Through analyzing the best economy index and its influence factors of tractor,a kind of economical shift rule is put forward,which based on the minimum fuel consumption rate of tractor. It requires not only the operating point of the engine located at the lowest fuel consumption zone,also need the tractor traction efficiency to be higher. For this reason,the slip rate of driving wheel is introduced to constitute economical shift rule and its control strategy,which takes the speed,drive wheel speed,engine speed,throttle opening and transmission gear ratio of tractor as control parameters. The fuzzy control is used to identify the driving intention,and the driver intervention on the shifting process is introduced to the transmission control,which can reflect the actual working environment of the tractor. Taking the YTO LA2004 wheeled tractor which equipped with automatic power shift transmission as investigative subject,the simulation analysis of light load working condition is carried out. The results show that the gear and throttle opening change with traction load,which ensure that the working point of the engine is in a low fuel consumption zone. The fuel consumption rate of tractor is reduced and the stability of the actual speed of the tractor is achieved. A theoretical basis for the development of automatic transmission control system of tractor is provided by the research

system.value: Research on Transmission Characteristic of ZF 9-speed Automatic Transmission

abstract.value: Taking the ZF 9-speed automatic transmission (9HP48) as the research object，the power transmission line in each gear of the automatic transmission is clarified. The transmission ratio and torque ratio (considering friction loss) of each gear are theoretically derived. The М.А.Крейнeс formula is used to calculate the transmission efficiency of 9 forward gears and 1 reverse gear. To verify the theoretical derivation，AMESim simulation software is used for building the simulation model of the automatic transmission. The transmission ratio and transmission efficiency values of each gear are obtained through the simulation calculation. The simulation results are consistent with the theoretical analysis results. The simulation results verify the correctness of the theoretical derivation and provide a basis for optimizing the automatic transmission scheme in the future

warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

If the pathway-aware selector uses MORE tests while achieving WORSE assurance, the clinical-pathway bridge adds complexity without value. informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-020: A sufficiency proof that is merely an integration of known statistical methods (NI testing + coverage + multiple-testing correction + sensitivity analysis) is NOT a novel mathematical result. Under §103, combining known methods to solve a problem the market explicitly asks for is likely obvious (KSR v. Teleflex). The frontier is a NEW MATHEMATICAL BOUND — e.g., a tight bound on minimum evidence set size that is better than what existing methods give individually, or a proof technique that connects clinical pathway coverage to statistical sufficiency in a way that is not derivable from existing theory. Additionally: killer tests for sufficiency proofs must include a TRUE POSITIVE case (sufficient evidence for a SAFE modification that the system correctly accepts), not just a true negative (insufficient evidence that the system correctly rejects).

informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-022: Synergy ≠ novelty and synergy ≠ commercial moat. A functional interaction (A changes B) is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT for invention. The interaction itself — the causal law, the emergent effect, and functional equivalents across domains — must survive prior art independently. Additionally: synergy claims without quantitative comparison against the STRONGEST baseline are stories, not evidence. The unexpected-effect proof requires: (1) pre-registered quantitative prediction, (2) strongest baseline identified, (3) killer experiment vs that baseline, (4) result not predictable from A and B independently. The new standard: A changes B → unexpected effect → interaction survives prior art → reproducible advantage → cannot be cheaply reproduced → buyer value.

custody_records.raw_content: The share of videos in the internet traffic has been growing, therefore understanding how videos capture attention on a global scale is also of growing importance. Most current research focus on modeling the number of views, but we argue that video engagement, or time spent watching is a more appropriate measure for resource allocation problems in attention, networking, and promotion activities. In this paper, we present a first large-scale measurement of video-level aggregate engagement from publicly available data streams, on a collection of 5.3 million YouTube videos published over two months in 2016. We study a set of metrics including time and the average percentage of a video watched. We define a new metric, relative engagement, that is calibrated against video properties and strongly correlate with recognized notions of quality. Moreover, we find that engagement measures of a video are stable over time, thus separating the concerns for modeling engagement and those for popularity -- the latter is known to be unstable over time and driven by external promotions. We also find engagement metrics predictable from a cold-start setup, having most of its variance explained by video context, topics and channel information -- R2=0.77. Our observations imply several prospective uses of engagement metrics -- choosing engaging topics for video production, or promoting engaging videos in recommender systems.

In recognizing that public outreach efforts affect career outcomes for young people, it is important to assess the demographics of those being reached and continually consider strategies for successfully engaging underrepresented groups. One such outreach event, the International Astronomical Youth Camp (IAYC), has a 50-year history and has reached ~1700 participants from around the world. We find that the IAYC is doing well in terms of gender (59% female, 4.7% non-binary at the most recent camp) and LGBT+ representation, whereas black and ethnic minorities are lacking.
